newsitem.title: CANADA: Emily Griffiths retires from WIC board.
newsitem.headline: Emily Griffiths retires from WIC board.

text.p: Emily Griffiths, matriarch of the family that controls WIC Western Broadcasting Ltd, said on Monday she was retiring from the broadcaster's board of directors.
She will be replaced by Ed Giacomelli, a managing director of investment firm Rothschild Canada Ltd.
Griffiths, 75, said in a news release that she wanted less direct involvement in WIC. She still controls a majority of WIC's voting shares.

WIC has faced intense shareholder pressure over a two-tier share structure that enables the Griffiths to control the company by owning a majority of its voting shares while holding only about seven percent of its total equity.
Dissident shareholders have criticized WIC's performance as mediocre and called for more independent directors.

Asked if Giacomelli was intended to be an independent voice on the board, a WIC spokesman referred queries to Klaus Priebe, a member of the Griffiths family and WIC's deputy chairman. Priebe was not immediately available for comment.
Giacomelli was also not available for comment.
Faced with several shareholder protest motions, WIC at its annual meeting earlier this year said it would consider adding an independent director to its board.

Oppenheimer and Co, the New York investment house that submitted the motions, said Monday it had little information about Giacomelli but did not consider his appointment to be a step toward meeting its demands.
"As far as we are concerned, this is not a response to what we requested at the annual meeting," Oppenheimer managing director Eric Rosenfeld said.
Emily Griffiths said Giacomelli "will further strengthen the board."
Priebe said the change demonstrated the family's "desire to attract high caliber outside professionals to WIC."
The family "is committed to ensuring WIC pursues opportunities that enhance the value of WIC for the benefit of all shareholders," added Frank W. Griffiths, son of the company's founder.
A WIC spokesman confirmed the change and said the company would issue a statement soon.
